You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like a post-COVID recovery period. Unemployment is high versus its 3-year average (+2.0) but falling fast (-2.0 over 3m). Payrolls are strong at +2.0 and the national activity index is high. Policy rate and 2-year yields are very low (-2.0), and inflation is low (-1.5) but rising. The 10y-2y spread is up sharply. Industrial production is still depressed but rebounding (+2.5 over 3m).

The 36-month window matters here. In mid-2020 the 3-year lookback would include the low-rate 2017-2019 period, and the policy rate would not be a -2 z-score. By late 2020, with rates at zero versus a 2018-2019 average of about 2%, -2.0 fits. Unemployment +2.0 with a 12m change of +2.0 fits late 2020 too, at roughly 6.7-6.9%. Payrolls averaging +2.0 z would fit a 3m average of about 1M in Sep-Nov 2020, while the activity index at +3.0 for the 3m change matches the rebound.

Equity returns are modest here, though, with the 12m return at only +1.0, and VIX is only +0.5. That suggests the VIX level was moderate. Headline CPI at -1.5 with core CPI at -1.5 fits 2020 too. A 10y yield at -1.5 fits. The dollar fell by -1.5 over 3m, matching H2 2020. Gold at +1.5 over 12m also fits.

Candidates are Oct-Dec 2020. The 1m treasury return of -1.0 and 10y yield change of +0.5 over 3m suggest a rate rise, which points to October or November 2020, with the 20y+ at -1.5 for 1m. The 3m change in the unemployment rate of -2.0 fits Oct 2020 (from 8.4% in Aug to 6.9% in Oct), and the 1m treasury selloff fits as well. The activity index 3m avg is high (+2.0) in Oct. Equity 1m at only +1.0 matches October 2020, when the S&P fell about 2.7%, but this snapshot looks stronger. November had a +11% S&P rise, which would be more than +1.0 z. October seems the better fit given the muted equity move, though VIX in October was high and the VIX 3m change is only -0.5. Dec 2020 is also possible, with IP weak.

I'll go with November 2020 as a compromise... Treasuries fell in November only mildly, whereas equities jumped. I'll choose October.
